headline: Approved property and motor vehicle tax refunds and board appointments; tabled 14 Community Development Block Grant agreements.
summary: Seven consent calendar items passed unanimously, including a plant donation for DeNicola Park and a funding agreement with Yale University for an opioid case manager. One resident spoke during public input, and the Town Clerk answered questions about the board and commission process.
decisions: Approved seven consent calendar items unanimously, including a plant donation and a Yale University funding agreement.
Approved board and commission appointments recommended by Mayor Sendroff, 13-2.
Approved refunds of property and motor vehicle taxes unanimously.
Tabled the New Business items, including 14 CDBG subrecipient agreements, 14-0-1.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL 
 
REGULAR MEETING  
AMENDED MINUTES DRAFT 
 
7:00 PM, NOVEMBER 16, 2026 
 
 
Present Katie Kiely, President 
Present Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Present - Sarah Gallagher, Maj Leader 
Present Bob Anthony, Min Leader 
Present Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Present Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
Present Maurine Crouch 
Present Doug Foley 
Present - Jeron Alston 
Present Abdul Osmanu 
Present - Rhonda Caldwell 
Present - Grace Teodosio 
Present - Adrian Webber 
Present - Ted Stevens 
Present Tameeka Parks 
  
Meeting Convenes 
 
  1. Roll Call, Pledge of Allegiance, Moment of Silence and Land Acknowledgment, 
followed by an introduction to the meeting.   
 
The Meeting was called to order at 7:01pm.     
Regular Agenda  
 
  2. Public Input Session was opened at 7:04pm with 1 member of the public coming to 
speak.  Public Comment was closed at approximately 7:08pm.   
  
  3. Consent Calendar 
Motion to approve: Cardwell 
Second: Gallagher  
       
 
a. Resolution to accept Plant Donation from Eli's Garden of Healing for 
DeNicola Park Passed out of Adim & Settlement 11/9. 
      
       
 
b. Reappointment of Mike Doyle to Veterans Commission. Passed out of IT & 
Civic Engagement 11/9 
      
       
 
c. Reappointment of Reginald Jackson to Veterans Commission Passed out 
of IT & Civic Engagement 11/9 
      
       
 
d. Order Authorizing Agreement with Vertosoft of OpenGov Software 
and Services Passed out of IT & Civic Engagement 11/9 
      
       
 
e. Order Authorizing an Agreement with Catalis Public Works & Citizen 
Engagement, LLC Hamden Police Department Passed out of Public Safety 11/9 
      
       
 
f. Order Authorizing Interdepartmental Transfer 2025-2026 Fiscal Year 
Budget - Mayor's Office/Public Works/Finance Passed out of Finance 11/9 
      
      
 
 
g. Order Approving a Funding Support Agreement with Yale University 
— Opioid Case Manager Passed out of Finance 11/9 
 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions. Passed Unanimously.
4. Reports 
President Kiely noted receipt of the ARPA Reports. No additional reports were 
provided for this evening’s meeting.  
  5. Communication Submissions 
President Kiely noted the upcoming submissions for referral  
  6. New Business 
      
 
 
a. Appointment of Board and Commission Members as Recommended 
by Mayor Sendroff in the Memo Dated October 21, 2026, Passed out of IT & 
Civic Engagement Committee 11/19 
Moved: Foley 
Second: Parks 
Vote: 13 in favor, 2 Opposed (Anthony, Caldwell) 0 abstentions. Item 
passed 
 
The Town Clerk joined the Zoom to answer any questions the council 
members had on the Board & Commission process.  She also provided 
an overview of the various marketing efforts she conducts to advertise 
openings on the Boards/Commissions. 
 
 
Items b, c, d 
      
       
 
b. Refund of Property Taxes Collected Between 07/01/2026-06/30/2027.  
      
       
 
c. Refund of Property and Motor Vehicle Taxes Collected Prior to 
07/01/2026 
      
      
 
 
d. Refund of Motor Vehicle Taxes Collected Between 07/01/2026 - 
06/30/2027 
 
Council President Kiely requested a motion to bundle items b, c, and d 
Motion: Anthony 
Second: Figlar 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions. Motion to bundle passed. 
 
Council President then requested a motion to move items b, c, d. 
Motion; Foley 
Second: Cardwell 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Items passed unanimously 
  
      
  7. Recess is called for Regular LC Council Committees to convene (No vote is required 
for this action). 
 
Standing Committees Convene 
Due to a noticing glitch, President Kiely announced that the committees would not be meeting 
this evening.  She asked Attorney Gruen if she could add the items in section 5 of the 
Administration and Settlement agenda as well as the item from the Committee of the Whole to 
New Business within the Legislative Council agenda.  Attorney Gruen confirmed that it could 
be done with a 2/3rds vote.
Attorney Gruen said that items 15, 16 and 17 from the Administration and Settlement 
Committee were not ready to be heard and noted that it would not be appropriate to bring 
them over this evening. 
 
President Kiely requested a motion to add items 1-14 from section 5 of the Administration and 
Settlement agenda, as well as the one item from the Committee of the Whole to the 
Legislative Council agenda’s New Business.

Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Cardwell 
Vote: (2/3rds needed):  In favor 10: Kiely, Cardwell, Gallagher, Hunt, Figlar, Alston, Caldwell, 
Webber Stevens, and Parks.  Opposed 2: Crouch, Osmanu, Foley, Teodosio.  Abstention 1: 
Anthony.  Motion to add items passes.
After a brief discussion, Council member Figlar made a motion to table the New Business 
items 
Second: Hunt

Caldwell, Teodosio, Webber, Stevens, & Parks), 0 opposed, 1 abstention (Anthony)   
ADJOURNMENT 
With no additional business before the Council, President Kiely called for a motion to adjourn 
Motion: Cardwell 
Second: Hunt 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:21pm.
